subject.title: fix(gateway): MCP clients receive responses for JSON-RPC notifications

question: Should OpenClaw accept the spec-aligned MCP loopback change from JSON responses to HTTP 202 empty bodies for id-less JSON-RPC messages after the mixed-batch error path is fixed?
rationale: The protocol contract supports the change, but it alters externally observable loopback HTTP behavior for existing clients and should be an intentional Gateway/MCP compatibility decision.

options.title: Accept Spec-Aligned Notifications
options.body: Merge after the mixed-batch error path is fixed so id-less notifications never receive JSON-RPC responses while request messages still do.

options.title: Preserve Legacy Responses
options.body: Ask for a compatibility-preserving design if existing loopback clients must keep receiving response bodies for id-less methods.

options.title: Pause For Gateway Policy
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers define a broader raw MCP HTTP notification and batch-error policy.

recommendation.title: Accept Spec-Aligned Notifications
recommendation.body: Merge after the mixed-batch error path is fixed so id-less notifications never receive JSON-RPC responses while request messages still do.

likelyOwner.reason: shakkernerd has the strongest recent Gateway/MCP loopback transport history signal for this response-contract surface.
